arXiv:2409.00702 is **“MARS: Matching Attribute-aware Representations for Text-based Sequential Recommendation”** (Kim et al., CIKM 2024). Uses title, brand, and category as textual key–value attributes; a shared pretrained Longformer-base encodes candidate items and reversed interaction histories. Projected token states are averaged within each attribute, producing multiple vectors. Scoring sums attribute-wise maximum cosine similarities across historical items. Training uses temperature-scaled cross-entropy and two stages, eventually fixing item embeddings. [Paper, §§2–3](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.00702v2)

Ablations compare attribute representations against single [BOS] vectors and item-level average pooling, and replace MaxSim with mean matching. Full MARS wins across the five evaluated datasets in Table 3; these comparisons support fine-grained attribute encoding and selective matching, but do not isolate the contribution of pretrained initialization. For this RecHarness task, brand/category metadata and fetched pretrained weights are unavailable or prohibited. A title/description encoder trained from scratch within HSTU would therefore be an adaptation, not a reproduction of MARS; attribute-aware representation and matching alone are already established prior art. [Ablations, §3.2 and Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.00702v2#S3.SS2)
